Subject: Invoice 9471 - partial EUR / partial USD payment — wire routing question

Hi Mina,

We received invoice 9471 and are ready to initiate payment, but internal treasury flagged a split-settlement situation: our procurement team will pay the EUR portion via SEPA, but one department will pay the USD portion from a US entity (they will send a USD wire).

Questions:
- For the USD leg, will Redwood accept a correspondent (cover) payment or do you require beneficiary-pay? If correspondent, which intermediary bank/correspondent should our bank use so fees don't get netted unexpectedly?
- If intermediary fees are deducted on the USD leg, how should we document fee allocation for VAT reclaim (we need the invoice to show VAT base clearly)?

Attached: invoice_9471_globex.pdf

We'd like to avoid a double-charge where the USD intermediary eats part of the payable and forces a disputed short-pay. Any guidance or a bank-wire CSV template from your side would help.

Thanks,
Andreas

Hi Andreas,

Quick clarifications from Finance:
- VAT / invoice: to support EU VAT reclaim, we need the invoice to explicitly show the VAT base and include Globex AG's VAT ID and our EU VAT ID (see line 4 of invoice). If VAT is charged, we cannot accept a netted fee that reduces the VAT base unless we issue a credit note reflecting the gross amount.
- USD leg: correspondent (cover) wires often result in a single intermediary deduction between correspondent and beneficiary bank. If that deduction happens, the payer typically cannot provide a separate fee invoice that ties to the transaction for VAT reclaim — it becomes messy.

Recommended options (ranked):
1) On-net: payer sends USD via a US our-nostro (ACH/wire to our US bank) — no correspondent fees.
2) Cover payment using the correspondent in the attached collection-routing-spec.xlsx (use field C6). In this case, request the paying bank to set the cover instruction so fees are borne by the payer (suffix 'OUR' when possible) and include the intermediary's trace/reference.
3) Beneficiary-pay (SHA/BEN): acceptable but please be explicit in remittance that the gross amount must be reflected on the invoice for VAT purposes; Redwood will then issue a short credit if intermediary fees materially change the VAT base.

Concession for this invoice: because this is a multi-entity split and to avoid delays, Redwood will absorb intermediary fees up to EUR 15 per transaction for May 2028 settlement only. If fees exceed that, we'll request documentation to support a one-time reimbursement or a credit note.

I've uploaded the bank-wire template and routing spec to our drive: https://drive.redwood.com/shared/collections/DEAL-9471-routing-spec — the template includes the correspondent bank, SWIFT/BIC, and the expected remittance string to avoid short-pays.

Attachments: collection-routing-spec.xlsx (see tab "Correspondents")

Regards,
Laura Bennett
Director, Finance Operations | Redwood Inference
laura.bennett@redwood.com

Mina / Laura,

Thanks for the detailed options — helpful. A couple of clarifying points from our side: 
- The US payer cannot reach your US nostro for operational reasons; they must send an international USD wire from a US bank that will route via a correspondent.
- They can mark fees as OUR if their treasury is willing, but treasury needs the exact correspondent details and the intermediary BIC to include in the instruction. We see that in C6 — we'll produce a cover instruction.

One more: if the USD intermediary deducts an amount (e.g., $22), would Redwood issue a credit note to restore the VAT base (so we can reclaim VAT) or would you prefer to net that from the outstanding balance? We need clarity to coordinate our GL.

If possible, can Redwood issue the credit note once you receive proof of intermediary deduction (SWIFT MT103 and the payer’s bank fee line)? That will allow our accounting to reflect the gross settlement and support VAT reclaim.

Appreciate the EUR concession offer for May — that helps. We'll aim to set fees OUR and use the correspondent listed, but want the contingency plan documented.

Best,
Andreas

Andreas — thanks, that plan works. Confirming final process so treasury has a clear path: 

1) Please instruct the USD payer to send a cover payment and use the correspondent entry in C6 of the attached template. Ask the sending bank to set charges to OUR and include the intermediary BIC and trace/reference.

2) If intermediary fees are deducted despite OUR instructions, please forward the MT103 / payment trace and the payer's bank fee confirmation to finance@redwood.com. Upon receipt, Redwood Finance will:
   - Issue a credit note equal to the intermediary deduction amount to restore the VAT base for reclaim purposes; OR
   - Reimburse up to EUR 15 per transaction directly (as noted previously) depending on the evidence provided and whether the deduction exceeds our concession threshold.

3) Please ensure the invoice includes Globex AG VAT ID and the VAT base line item. If any amounts are reclassified we will issue a credit note referencing invoice 9471 and Deal DEAL-9471.

I've also opened a DocuSign amendment for the payment terms (link below) in case you want the concession and credit-note process reflected in a short addendum: https://docusign.com/prepare/redirect/ABC-9471

Attachments: bank-wire-template.csv (for your treasury team)
